lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Fix the experience order.
Verify the 9-tonne figure and its measurement period.
400 to 1,150 is a 187.5% increase, not 150%.
Strengthen the causal basis for attributing the increase to reminders.
items.because: User interviews may explain why the feature was chosen, but they do not prove the feature caused the growth.

items.says: Clarify the time period over which weekly active users increased.
75% to 95% is a 20-percentage-point increase, not a 20% increase.
Explain how the volunteer shift system affected pickup-slot fill rate.
items.because: The mechanism is not immediately obvious.

items.says: Clarify whether the result was sustained and over what period.
Correct the RICE logic: Reach should represent the number of users, merchants, transactions, or another population affected over a defined period.
items.because: “Support tickets each feature would close” does not cleanly represent Reach and may signal weak product-method knowledge.

items.says: Include the period used for Reach; RICE scores are not meaningful without a defined time horizon.
Add an outcome from the prioritization.
items.because: Merely applying a framework is weaker than showing what decision it changed.

items.says: Add a clear subject and ownership; the sentence currently becomes grammatically indirect near the end.
Specify what problem or feature area became the priority.
Clarify how interview findings, chargeback analysis, and financial sizing affected the decision.
Consolidate with the preceding roadmap bullet unless they concern clearly different prioritization decisions.
items.because: This overlaps with the preceding roadmap bullet.

items.says: Remove this as a separate bullet because it duplicates the earlier conversion bullet.
Change the causal claim so it matches the unit of randomization and measurement.
items.because: Avoid generalizing session-level results to all merchant customers unless the analysis supports that inference.

items.says: Preserve any unique methodological detail by incorporating it into the stronger checkout bullet.
This bullet contains too many separate activities: implementation, SOPs, training, vendor negotiations, and labor savings.
Make the attribution for 1,800 saved hours clear. Explain whether it came from route optimization, process changes, or both.
Add adoption, number of drivers, route volume, cost savings, or service-level impact if available.
Consider splitting it only if both parts produced distinct, significant results and space permits.
Replace responsibility language with the decisions or improvements the scorecards enabled.
Quantify scope: number of carriers, regions, managers, shipment volume, or spend.
Explain whether the scorecards improved service, cost, on-time delivery, claims, or carrier accountability.
'The monthly review meeting that discussed them' is vague and adds little without an outcome.
Add the measurement period and baseline error rate if available.
items.because: A relative reduction without a baseline can be difficult to evaluate.

items.says: Clarify whether the reduction was sustained after retraining.
If the improvement affected labor cost, rework, customer complaints, or order accuracy, add the most relevant downstream impact.
Define the forecast-error metric if it was MAPE, bias, or another standard measure.
Specify the business scope: product categories, revenue, facilities, or region.
Clarify whether you created the consensus-forecast process or only facilitated it.
'12 consecutive quarters' demonstrates consistency, but it is less important than business scale; remove it if space is tight.
Add context for why 'under 5 days' is strong: compare it with a prior average, service target, or avoided downtime if available.
Clarify whether you personally completed the work, led it, or worked as part of a team.
items.because: The current wording may overstate individual ownership if jobs were collaborative.

items.says: If possible, quantify reliability after repair, repeat-failure rates, or economic impact.
items.because: Turnaround alone does not show repair quality.

items.says: Add scale, inspection results, compliance rate, uptime, defects prevented, or issues identified.
Reduce emphasis on recordkeeping unless the documentation materially improved inspection outcomes or compliance.
If no measurable result exists, this is the first bullet to replace or remove.
Clarify whether 2,300 merchants were actually exposed to the redesigned process or represented the broader pilot population.
Identify your ownership more precisely: discovery, requirements, coordination, experimentation, launch, or analysis.
Make sure the one-step verification process did not involve a tradeoff in fraud, compliance, or approval quality. If those guardrail metrics remained stable, include that fact.
Clarify whether the increase was statistically reliable and over what test period.
State the correct measurement unit. Because randomization occurred by session, the direct measured effect is on sessions, not necessarily unique customers.
If repeat users could appear in both variants, confirm whether that was handled analytically.
Connect it more directly to your earlier onboarding work so recruiters immediately understand that it is the downstream result of that initiative.
Clarify whether the additional rollout occurred or was only approved.
If the rollout produced later results, use those rather than stopping at approval.
Change the grammar from singular 'saving' to 'savings.'
Clearly distinguish projected savings from realized savings.
items.because: The current wording could be read as an achieved financial result even though it came from a model.

items.says: Add the major assumptions or cost categories behind the estimate if they establish credibility.
Change from passive voice to clear ownership.
Add a measurable result such as reduced form length, processing time, errors, or staff effort.
Clarify whether the shortened form was merely adopted or produced a demonstrated improvement.
If your team did the work collectively, accurately distinguish your contribution as team lead from the team’s output.
This duplicates the pilot approval mentioned in the first bullet.
Consolidate the approval into one place unless this bullet highlights a separate executive-presentation skill that is important for the role.
If retained, focus on what changed because of the presentation, not simply who attended.
Clarify whether the pilot was completed and whether results are available.
Keep only skills that are supported by bullets elsewhere.
Ensure 'A/B testing' reflects sound experimental practice, especially after correcting the session-level measurement issue.
'Roadmapping' will be more credible after fixing the RICE bullet and showing an actual prioritization decision.
Consider adding relevant product capabilities only if you genuinely have them, such as product analytics, prioritization, market research, stakeholder management, or KPI definition.
Avoid broad soft skills here.
Indicate proficiency only if it is meaningful and defensible.
Add analytics or technical tools only if you have actually used them; SQL is commonly screened for in product roles, but do not claim it without real competence.
Ensure Amplitude is reflected in the experience or project bullets if it played a meaningful role.
'Excel' is generic; its value is stronger if your experience demonstrates modeling, forecasting, or analysis.
Include prototyping, BI, or collaboration tools only when relevant to the jobs and genuinely used.
Use consistent date formatting and punctuation throughout.
Prevent bullets from breaking awkwardly across lines in the final PDF.
Keep bullet punctuation consistent—either periods on all bullets or none.
For product roles, prioritize Harbor Payments and the food-rescue app visually and in detail.
Keep the résumé to one page unless you have substantial additional relevant material.
Add a summary only if it efficiently explains the unusual transition from operations to MBA/product work to diesel mechanics.
items.because: Otherwise, let the ordering and bullet selection establish the narrative.

items.says: Tailor the skills and bullet emphasis to the target: product roles should foreground discovery, prioritization, experimentation, launch, adoption, and business impact.
